item.title: Aaron Rodgers pulls back curtain on bargaining talks with NFL envisioning one week of 16 international games
item.description: Aaron Rodgers revealed CBA talks once included a full international week with 16 games abroad, but says idea failed because of revenue concerns.
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Rodgers is an unrepentant fan of the NFL's international games and after the Pittsburgh Steelers won on Sunday in the league's first-ever game in France, the Steelers quarterback decided to offer a lesson on what those games abroad could have been if not for owners and the league not being so focused on money.

Rodgers, in his 22nd and final year in the league, reflected on past collective bargaining negotiations with the NFL after Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints and said opportunities were missed to make international games bigger.

"The reach of the league is fantastic, and I think I always wanted to be a part of it," Rodgers said. "I remember the 2011 CBA (collective bargaining agreement), there was talk about more games, expanding the amount of international games.

NFL OVERCOMES CIVIL UNREST, TRUMP CONCERNS AND CALLS TO POSTPONE AS STEELERS AND SAINTS KICK OFF IN PARIS

"Didn't really a whole lot until the second CBA, and there was talk about doing a week, an international week where you had games in 16 different places, and you just added an extra bye-week."

Wait, the NFL and NFL Players Association talked about having a full week of solely international games?

That might have caused something of a revolt among American NFL fans wanting to drive down the road to their local team's stadium and enjoy America's game – in America.

"So you'd play 16 regular-season games," Rodgers continued. "You have two bye weeks. One of those weeks would have been an international week. I think it'd been phenomenal for the game."

NFL FIELD EXPERT SAYS PLAYING INTERNATIONAL GAME ON BRAZIL FIELD 'CHALLENGING' AND INCLUDED TRIM WITH SCISSORS

Not in America, but tell us more, Aaron. Tell us about the current situation.

"Now that the owners want to push for 17 games for the, you know, extra revenue and because they care so much about player safety, it [the international week] would have been nice," Rodgers said.

Did you notice the passive-aggressive dig at NFL owners? But back to Aaron's wish for the international week to have come to pass:

SOLD OUT MELBOURNE CROWD STANDS FOR 25TH ANNIVERSARY COMMEMORATION OF 9/11 AT NFL'S FIRST AUSTRALIA GAME

"I think there's 16 opportunities," he said. "I mean, you could do obviously in Canada, you could do in Mexico. There's been games in Brazil. You could probably open up another country in South America.

"Obviously, there's a lot of opportunities in Europe, you know, Ireland, fantastic, France, Spain, Germany, multiple games in England. And then who knows?"

EXCLUSIVE: SECRETARY OF STATE MARCO RUBIO GIVES NFL COMMISSIONER ASSURANCES THAT GAME IN FRANCE 'WILL BE FINE'

The "who knows," in Rodgers' mind, includes playing in more exotic venues abroad.

"There's, uh, you know, Dubai," he said. "That area has really gotten into the sporting world in a number of ways. You got a boxing and UFC, I think was there yesterday, I believe.

NFL MONITORS FRANCE STREET VIOLENCE BEFORE SAINTS-STEELERS GAME NEAR PARIS WITH A MAJOR DECISION LOOMING

"So I think there's great opportunities for expansion in those things. It'd be awesome to see them have that international week. Because I think it's great for the game and the expansion of the game."

Despite the fact Rodgers is a major fan of playing games abroad, he does wish the league and its owners would agree to set parameters for them that include travel. The NFL was asked about that possibility last week and was against the idea of imposing travel mandates on individual teams.

But commissioner Rodgers would do it – once he's done taking another jab at those money-grubbing owners.

"I wish there was a mandate, though, from the league, and they would have to open up their pocketbooks too, which, you know, maybe they'll look tight on money and stuff," Rodgers said.

"But, I think they should mandate every team coming over Sunday or Monday to really enjoy the culture and the place you're going. And you can do events in those cities and outreach stuff in community work.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

"But they won't because they're a little tight."

That's truly something when one of the NFL's biggest names and something of an ambassador for the game wants to play an entire week's schedule abroad, but in the next breath says the NFL will never do it because the owners and the league are too cheap.

item.title: Sharpen memory and fight brain fog with simple 60-second trick from a neurologist
item.description: Dr. Rhonda Voskuhl explains why crosswords and sudoku miss the mark for brain fog and which timed word games actually target verbal memory loss.
item.content:encoded:
Brain games, crosswords and math puzzles are often promoted as ways to sharpen memory, but neurologists warn that generic exercises may not address the specific cause of mental fog.

Dr. Rhonda Voskuhl, a professor of neurology at UCLA and co-founder of Cleopatra RX in Los Angeles, says brain exercises only work if they target the specific mental function that is slowing down.

"You can’t just do random cognitive exercises," Voskuhl told Fox News Digital at the Livelong Women’s Health Summit in New York City in September. "They’ve got to fit the problem."

DOCTOR REVEALS '10-YEAR RULE' FOR EVALUATING BRAIN FOG AND DEMENTIA SYMPTOMS

The problem, she said, is verbal memory. "Doing math is not going to help … You need an exercise that will help you with words."

Mental fog — especially the kind triggered by midlife hormone changes during perimenopause and menopause — impacts very specific areas of the brain, according to Voskuhl.

When estrogen levels drop, overall intelligence and basic logic remain completely normal. Instead, the brain takes a hit in two main areas: verbal memory (recalling names and words) and processing speed (thinking quickly under pressure), experts say.

FORGETTING NAMES AND LOSING KEYS MAY SIGNAL SOMETHING OTHER THAN DEMENTIA

Games like Sudoku and other number puzzles primarily exercise logic and math skills, so they may not improve word-recall difficulties.

"It’s not a global problem with the brain," Voskuhl said. "It’s not global brain atrophy, but there are some regions on MRIs and research studies that show that the hippocampus, the memory area, will have some atrophies, some functional connection issues."

To understand why word-based exercises may help, it is useful to distinguish between the following two stages of memory, experts say.

DAILY EATING HABIT LINKED TO BETTER BRAIN HEALTH IN OLDER ADULTS, NEW RESEARCH SUGGESTS

Brain fog typically affects retrieval, not encoding. The word or name is still stored safely in the memory, but the brain's search engine is running slowly.

To effectively target brain fog, Voskuhl says exercises need to focus on two things: finding words and working quickly.

"It’s basically processing speed," she said. "So you need an exercise that is going to be something that makes you rush, makes you do it quickly."

The following types of exercises target processing speed and active word recall.

Instead of using generic puzzle apps, Voskuhl recommends paying attention to where you stumble in daily life and picking games that match those challenges.

People "know themselves," she said — "what they are bad at or what they used to be good at and now they’re not as good at ... Once you know those things, you should think about what kind of games [to play]. You can play around with different games. You can see if it pushes you."

item.title: Brandi Glanville says doctors are 'taking my face off' in exploratory surgery after years of health issues
item.description: Brandi Glanville details the $5,000 exploratory surgery to remove what she believes is something alive moving beneath the skin on her face.
item.content:encoded:
Brandi Glanville is taking a major step in her ongoing health battle by going under the knife.

During an episode of her "Brandi Glanville Unfiltered" podcast, shared on Thursday, Oct. 22, the 53-year-old reality star went into detail about the "exploratory surgery" she is scheduled to have on Friday.

"Dr. Carlo Honrado is taking my face off on Friday and going to do an exploratory surgery to kind of do a power wash under my skin," she said. "And then he knows where there's two definite spots, like either fungal balls or something alive. I think it's alive personally cause it moves when it wants."

She explained that after four years of dealing with the issue, she is "super excited" but also "scared to death" because she has "never had facial surgery" and has heard the procedure is "more intensive than a facelift."

FORMER REALITY STAR OPENS UP ABOUT NEW DIAGNOSIS AFTER YEARS-LONG HEALTH ORDEAL

While she is nervous, Glanville is hopeful the surgery will be a success, as facial plastic and reconstructive surgeon, Dr. Honrado, "comes highly recommended." She noted that she is "okay" with the $5,000 price tag, telling herself, "what if he actually does take it out and it's done?"

"It started in my face, my cheek and my jawbone, and then it went over my head back in my neck. Now it's down my spine," she explained.

She went on to say that the doctor told her if he is able to "cut that head off the beast", getting rid of the rest of it will be more manageable.

Glanville previously shared that she believed she picked up a parasite after visiting Morocco in 2023. She suffered from facial paralysis and was initially diagnosed with stress-induced angioedema.

In September, she revealed she had been diagnosed with highly resistant ESBL Klebsiella and Enterobacter with biofilm, coccidioidomycosis, also known as Valley fever, Demodex dermatitis and mononucleosis, noting her treatment includes daily IV treatments which she estimated would cost $3,300 to $6,000 a month.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the "Real Housewives of Beverly Hills" alum revealed she agreed to compete on the current season of "Special Forces" because she needed the money after years of spending on medical treatments.

"The medical system here is broken," Glanville explained. "So I have, like, from 8 a.m. on, I have creditors from, like, medical things calling me, like from Cedars-Sinai. It's out of control. Like I spent hundreds of thousands of dollars that I had saved. I emptied my 401(k). And it's all for medical bills. And I had insurance, and they told me nothing was wrong. I'm so angry. You know, going into my mid-fifties I had a cushion and that's gone. So it's very scary right now."

In addition to her financial situation, Glanville explained she agreed to participate on the show because she was in a place in her life where she "needed to prove to myself that I could do it again."

"I just want this s--- out of my body," Glanville wrote in September. "I want my health back. I want my life back. I want to feel like me again."

item.title: Giants' Cam Skattebo hit with penalty after crushing Texans defender on routine run
item.description: Cam Skattebo lowered his helmet and trucked a Houston Texans defender, drawing a controversial unnecessary roughness flag that left Harbaugh perplexed.
item.content:encoded:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is known for being a bit of a loose cannon on the football field.

He runs hard and crashes into defenders left and right. On Sunday, NFL officials suggested he crossed a line while trying to truck over a Houston Texans player.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Skattebo took a handoff from quarterback J.J. McCarthy in the first quarter. Skattebo found a crease, lowered his helmet and ran over an opposing defender. The running back put his head down and collided with safety M.J. Stewart.

A flag was thrown on the play and Skattebo was called for unnecessary roughness because he lowered his helmet.

It’s really unclear what Skattebo was supposed to do in that situation. Helmet-to-helmet crashes happen in the NFL and usually a flag is thrown if the player on the receiving end of the damage is considered to be a defenseless player or a defender leads with their helmet when making a tackle – not the opposite. Even Giants head coach John Harbaugh seemed perplexed.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Giants and Texans were in a tight matchup in Week 7. The two teams were tied going into the half 14-14.

Skattebo had come under the microscope because he had no carries against the New Orleans Saints in Week 6. The Giants appeared to make some kind of point with Skattebo’s inaction. Harbaugh insisted last week he didn’t bench Skattebo.

"It wasn’t by design for him not to carry the ball," Harbaugh said. "Just when he was in there, we didn’t call any runs. You’re not thinking about which back is in the game and how many runs they’re getting. It’s we were going to give them all an equal shot, give them a chance, see who got a hot hand maybe, see who could get going with it. We weren’t planning on being down by 24, that’s for sure."

Skattebo’s fumbles have been a cause for concern but probably not enough to warrant a benching. He was certainly back in the offense in Week 7.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Firehouse Subs co-founder dies after building beloved American sandwich chain with brother
item.description: Chris Sorensen co-founded Firehouse Subs in Jacksonville, Florida, with less than $100 in the bank before building a 1,200-location empire.
item.content:encoded:
Chris Sorensen, a co-founder of the sandwich chain Firehouse Subs, has died at 65.

Before entering the restaurant industry, Sorensen was a professional guitarist, even sitting in with bands including Huey Lewis and the News, Lynyrd Skynyrd, Foreigner and Earth, Wind & Fire, according to his obituary.

He went on to become a firefighter, following in the footsteps of his father, Robert.

EVERY BITE COUNTS AS SANDWICH SHOP DITCHES TRADITIONAL SUB-BUILDING METHOD

After working at the Brevard County Fire Department and the Jacksonville International Airport Fire and Rescue Department, Chris spent 10 years as an engineer and EMT at the Jacksonville Fire and Rescue Department, where his dad also worked at the time.

In 1994, Chris and his younger brother, Robin, co-founded Firehouse Subs, opening the first location in their hometown of Jacksonville.

They had less than $100 in their checking accounts at the time, according to Nation’s Restaurant News.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Surprisingly, the first-ever order at the chain’s flagship location was not a sub, but two hot dogs with everything on them, which consisted of about 10 ingredients, Robin Sorensen told the Jacksonville Daily Record in 2020.

"We were so focused on the subs, we weren’t prepared for that order. Needless to say, it was a long ticket time," he said.

Featuring steamed meats and cheeses piled high on warm toasted rolls, Firehouse sandwiches soon became a hit.

Chris took creative ownership of the interior of Firehouse Subs restaurants, outfitting each location with a custom mural depicting fire and police service unique to the restaurant’s town.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

A collector of historical artifacts, he ensured that the legacy of Firehouse Subs was preserved, serving as the chain's unofficial archivist.

After being sold in 2021 for one billion dollars to Restaurant Brands International, which also owns Burger King, the Firehouse Subs fleet grew to more than 1,200 locations.

In 2005, Chris and Robin Sorensen created the Firehouse Subs Public Safety Foundation, with a mission of providing first-responders with life-saving equipment, tools and education.

The organization has awarded more than 118 million dollars in grants to 7,700 departments in the U.S. and Canada, per the obituary.

item.title: Country star Cody Johnson says Nashville wanted to change him before success
item.description: Cody Johnson walked away from a Nashville record deal after executives told him to ditch his cowboy hat, then spent a decade proving them wrong.
item.content:encoded:
Nashville wanted Cody Johnson to ditch his cowboy hat before giving him a shot at country music stardom.

The Texas-born country star said he walked away from a record deal after executives suggested he swap his signature cowboy look for a baseball cap — a move he viewed as a demand to change who he was before he could make it in the music business.

"They wanted a baseball cap, which I have nothing against, but it was the approach. It was the 'you're great, but once we change you, you'll make it.' And it pissed me off," he said in an interview with "CBS Mornings." "I tipped my hat and said, 'Thank you for your time.'"

CARRIE UNDERWOOD SAYS HER FAMILY COULD BE 'SELF-SUSTAINED' ON TENNESSEE FARM AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD SPOTLIGHT

It was a gamble that could have cost him his shot at stardom.

Instead, Johnson spent the next 10 years building a career on his own terms, playing bars and honky-tonks before becoming one of country music's biggest stars.

During his interview, Johnson spoke candidly about his rise to fame and the years of work behind his success.

COUNTRY SINGER CODY JOHNSON FORCED TO STOP 'GOD BLESS AMERICA' PERFORMANCE AS VIOLENT BRAWL BREAKS OUT

Long before arena crowds and industry recognition, the singer was a small-town Texas kid who dreamed of becoming a rodeo star.

He eventually traded bull riding for music after years of injuries and setbacks and selling CDs in rodeo parking lots as he tried to build a following.

The country star also struggled to believe his ambitions were within reach.

THOMAS RHETT REVEALS WHY HE AND WIFE LAUREN REJECT CELEBRITY PERKS FOR COUNTRY LIFE

"Truthfully, in my core, I didn't feel I was capable of attaining a goal that big, you know, to be a huge country music star, to own a cattle ranch," Johnson said.

After turning down the label opportunity, he spent years playing small venues, struggling financially and spending long stretches away from his family to keep his career alive.

"The pressure of knowing that you don't know how to pay your water bill, and you've just been on the road for a month and haven't seen your wife or your child, and you have nothing to show for it. That's that's tough to look in the mirror."

He continued, "I think that I just had decided at that point that no matter what, no matter how hard, no matter how high the mountain, I will not back down. I will not quit."

After a decade of grinding it out as an independent artist, Johnson saw record labels return with another opportunity — this time, he said, without the same demand to change his image.

"I just get to be myself and be authentic," he said.

Johnson has built a national following, sold out arenas and earned a place among country music's leading performers, while keeping the cowboy image he refused to abandon.

He and his wife, Brandi, have been married for more than a decade. They have three children: two daughters and a son.

item.title: Week 8 AP Top 25 Poll sees Big Ten gain equal footing on SEC and unbeaten Utah earn major respect
item.description: BYU dropped six spots after a double-overtime loss to UCF, while Texas jumped eight places in the latest AP Top 25 college football rankings.
item.content:encoded:
While Week 8 of the college football season couldn't possibly live up to the total chaos that unfolded the week prior, we still saw three Top 10 teams in the country all fall on the road, which has yet again resulted in some serious shuffling in the latest AP Top 25 Poll.

To no surprise, the biggest faller in this week's poll belongs to the BYU Cougars, who dropped six spots to No. 8 after losing to UCF on the road in double overtime. On the other side of the spectrum, Texas is this week's biggest jumper, with the Longhorns moving up eight spots to No. 11 after holding on and beating Ole Miss at home, 34-27.

Outside of Miami holding down the No. 1 spot for the second consecutive week, every team featured in the Top 20 this week has a new number next to their name.

The Big 12 saw a bit of cannibalization in Week 8, but when all the dust settled, Utah improved to 7-0 on the year after its late-night win over Houston, and was rewarded by moving up to No. 6 in the nation. Next up for the Utes is a huge matchup at Cincinnati, the same Cincinnati team that knocked off No. 8 Texas Tech on Saturday in a stunner.

Utah received one first-place vote in Week 8, while Ohio State picked up 10, and the Hurricanes earned 59.

Meanwhile, the Big Ten and the SEC each have three teams inside the latest Top 10, and as absolutely nobody saw coming, UCLA and Kentucky sit at No. 7 and No. 9, respectively, with just five weeks left in the regular season.

The upcoming college football Saturday happens to fall on Halloween, and it should be a doozy.

item.title: Buccaneers collect two freakish first-half scores to dominate Panthers – and, oh, Baker Mayfield is back
item.description: Calijah Kancey's 32-yard fumble return and Zyon McCollum's blocked extra point conversion powers the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' dominant first half.
item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are scoring points in the most unorthodox ways against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.

The Bucs led the Panthers convincingly with a 33-6 lead at halftime and 8 of their points came in freakish fashion.

The freakish fashion?

A defensive two-point conversion by cornerback Zyon McCullom.

A big-man touchdown fumble return by 280-pound defensive tackle Calijah Kancey.

Not typical.

BAKER MAYFIELD LEAVES GAME AFTER WRITHING IN PAIN ON TURF IN TAMPA BAY WHEN THUMB ON THROWING HAND INJURED

Let's begin with the Kancey score first. The Bucs have so far smothered the Panthers' offense and evidence of that was Al-Quadin Muhammad's strip-sack of Carolina quarterback Bryce Young.

Well, if you got a strip, you've got a loose football and Kancey scooped up the loose ball on a bounce, outran an offensive lineman 32 yards to the end zone and completed the score by performing a flip over the goal line.

None of that is typical big man behavior.

BAKER MAYFIELD LOSES BET TO COACH TODD BOWLES, HAS 'ROUGH COUPLE OF DAYS' INCLUDING AT PRESS CONFERENCE

This is dream-of-a-lifetime stuff for any defensive player. It's practically unheard of for a defensive lineman.

And, interestingly, Kancey's rare moment was not the most unorthodox of this game for the Bucs.

We present McCollum's two-pointer.

The Panthers had cut the deficit with a 50-yard hookup between Young and tight end Darren Waller. That cut Tampa Bay's lead to 17-6.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

But on the ensuing extra point, McCullom snatched a blocked extra point out of the air and returned it for, well, a conversion for the Bucs.

Two points.

Zany.

McCollum, by the way, is having a day. He also intercepted Young later in the first half.

The Bucs are in last place in the NFC South with a 1-5 record. But Baker Mayfield started this game after missing the previous three games with a dislocated thumb on his right (throwing) hand.

Mayfield threw a touchdown pass to Tez Johnson to give the Bucs a 33-6 halftime lead. Tampa Bay's 33 first-half points is the third-most in franchise history and most since 2021.

Thanks, weirdo points.

The Panthers, who have allowed eight points in the most unorthodox way, came into the game leading the NFC South with a 3-2 record.

item.title: MAPPED: The states Trump and top Democrats are targeting before Election Day
item.description: With Election Day less than two weeks away, Trump rallied in Florida, Georgia and Michigan as both parties deploy top surrogates to battlegrounds.
item.content:encoded:
With just nine days until Election Day, both parties are making a final push to shape the fight for control of Congress.

President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance are rallying Republicans across the country, while former President Barack Obama and former Vice President Kamala Harris are campaigning for Democrats.

The map traces their campaign stops so far this month, with states visited by both sides shaded gray.

Trump’s stops span the country, from Texas and Oklahoma to Ohio, Georgia, Florida and Michigan. He said in early October he planned to hold five to seven rallies a week. This weekend, he campaigned in Florida on Friday, Georgia on Saturday and Michigan on Sunday.

HIGH PRICES PUT TRUMP’S ECONOMY IN THE SPOTLIGHT AS THE GOP FIGHTS TO HOLD CONGRESS

The map includes both reliably Republican states and states with competitive races. Oklahoma and Alabama, for example, are deep-red states where rallies can help energize the GOP base.

Ohio, Texas and Iowa have competitive Senate contests; recent Cook Political Report polling showed Democratic candidates narrowly ahead in all three. Michigan is also a key Senate battleground.

REPUBLICANS JUST GOT A POWERFUL NEW PLAYBOOK FOR THE BATTLE FOR CONGRESS. HERE'S WHAT'S INSIDE.

The stops by Obama and Harris show Democrats are also leaning on well-known figures in states with consequential races.

Obama campaigned in Ohio and Michigan, while Harris’s recent appearances included Nevada, Mississippi and New Hampshire.

The map tracks campaign travel, not a formal ranking of battlegrounds. However, it offers a snapshot of where the parties are trying to rally voters in the final stretch before Nov. 3.

item.title: Parker McCollum wants his sons to learn the lesson hunting and ranch life taught him growing up
item.description: Parker McCollum recalls childhood hunting trips with his dad in Texas and reveals how he's passing that same love of the outdoors to his two sons.
item.content:encoded:
Parker McCollum has come a long way from the little boy who couldn't wait to tag along on hunting trips with his dad. Now, with two sons of his own, the country music star is looking forward to being on the other side of those childhood memories.

And he's already getting a head start.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

McCollum, who welcomed his second son with wife Hallie Ray in July, recently spent several days at the family ranch with his oldest boy, 2-year-old Major.

"I was taking him with me to kind of, you know, just do some ranch stuff," McCollum told OutKick OutDoors in an exclusive interview. "He can't really. He just kind of stands out there and pulls grass out of the ground while I'm working or whatever."

Major might not be much help around the ranch just yet, but McCollum certainly doesn't mind. After all, he remembers exactly what it was like to be that little boy.

Watch Parker McCollum's whole interview with OutKick OutDoors here:

"I remember those days so vividly," he said. "My dad would get me out of school early on a Friday to go down to the lease or the ranch or whatever, and we would let it rip all weekend. And a lot of times it was just him and I.

"To say that I look forward to doing that for him and with him is an understatement."

Hunting has been part of McCollum's life for as long as he can remember.

In a 2022 interview with NRA Country, the Texas native recalled going bird hunting with his father when he was around 8 years old, carrying a single-shot .410 shotgun. He also identified his dad as one of his favorite hunting buddies.

But McCollum's love for the outdoors started even before he was old enough to participate.

During a 2024 interview with Audacy, McCollum remembered crying when his father and other family members left for hunting trips without him because he was too young to come along.

Once he finally got his chance, he was hooked.

CHARTER CAPTAIN JONATHAN MOSS EXPLAINS HOW TO GET KIDS HOOKED ON FISHING FROM AN EARLY AGE

That outdoors-centered upbringing extended beyond hunting season, too. McCollum spent summers working cattle, branding steers and tending to his grandfather's ranch alongside his cousins.

Now he's hoping Major and his younger brother, Rocker, will grow up with that same appreciation for the outdoors.

And for McCollum, it's about much more than harvesting deer.

With a demanding music career, two young children and a schedule that often keeps him on the road, McCollum understands how difficult it can be to slow down.

That's exactly why he believes time outdoors is so important.

"There is nothing I love more than sitting in a tree in East Texas or South Texas or the Midwest. Even if you don’t see a dadgum deer," he told OutKick OutDoors. "There's just something about it that's so good for your soul."

McCollum explained that his family's trips to the ranch aren’t about checking things off a to-do list or packing as much activity into the day as possible.

"Our whole intention was just slowing it down and turning it off and just spending time as a family, and no agenda," he said. "We wake up late and cook breakfast, and hunt in the evenings, and crockpot dinner, and ride around."

It's a deliberate departure from the pace of everyday life — one McCollum says is becoming increasingly difficult to escape.

And that's precisely the lesson he hopes his sons will carry into adulthood.

"Don't ever get so busy or worried about other stuff that you forget to do this."

We couldn’t have said it better ourselves.

item.title: Winless Dolphins end historic drought and they did it against the almost-as-hapless Jets
item.description: The Miami Dolphins finally held their first lead of the 2025 NFL season against the New York Jets after running 293 offensive snaps without one.
item.content:encoded:
The Miami Dolphins were winless going into Sunday's Week 7 of the NFL season but it was much worse than that for the once storied franchise because coach Jeff Hafley's team had not held a lead all season.

The Dolphins had run 293 offensive snaps and not enjoyed an advantage at any point in any of them. But ...

BREAKING: The Dolphins took a 7-0 lead on the New York Jets on Sunday.

FALCONS QB TUA TAGOVAILOA BOOED BY DOLPHINS FANS AS MIAMI PAYS PRICE FOR FAILED RELATIONSHIP

The Dolphins had been the only team in the Super Bowl era to fail to hold a lead through their first five losses of the season.

As they say in Miami, no bueno.

But the Dolphins took the opening kickoff on a sunny, cool day at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey and marched 76 yards in seven plays to take their first lead of the season on a 7 yard pass from quarterback Malik Willis to rookie receiver Caleb Douglas.

Good for the Dolphins. It can be argued as improvement.

FANS RIP BENGALS' JORDAN BATTLE FOR GIVING FREE SCOUTING REPORT ON MALIK WILLIS BEFORE DOLPHINS MATCHUP

item.title: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado makes surprise return home after nearly a year abroad
item.description: María Corina Machado's return to Venezuela could reshape opposition dynamics as Edmundo González vows to join her and push for democratic elections.
item.content:encoded:
Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado made returned to her home country on Sunday after nearly a year abroad, re-entering a political landscape transformed by the U.S. ouster of Nicolás Maduro.

"I'm here. With you all," Machado wrote on social media, announcing her return for the first time since December. Her homecoming comes as Venezuela remains under the leadership of acting President Delcy Rodríguez, a longtime Maduro ally backed by the Trump administration, with no presidential election scheduled.

President Donald Trump, asked about Machado's return by reporters in Port Huron, Michigan, said he was unaware of the development but expressed hope for her safety.

TRUMP TOUTS ACCESS TO 65 BILLION BARRELS OF VENEZUELAN OIL IN DEAL HE SAYS WILL SLASH GAS PRICES

"I don't know anything about it, but I think she's a very nice woman," Trump said. "She gave me her Nobel Prize. So how can I say anything else? And I hope she's safe. She's a very nice woman. But we're doing really well in Venezuela."

Machado, who was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2025 for her peaceful opposition to Maduro's government, did not disclose her exact location or provide details about how she returned.

Fellow opposition leader Edmundo González, who ran for president in 2024 after Machado was barred from seeking office, confirmed her arrival on social media and said he would join her "very soon."

"Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!" González wrote on X. "You know it, this is until the end."

Machado's return comes nearly 10 months after U.S. forces captured Maduro in January, removing the longtime leader from power.

Rodríguez, Maduro's former vice president, has remained in power with the Trump administration's support, despite exceeding the period she was initially authorized to serve as acting president.

Trump has repeatedly praised his administration's relationship with Rodríguez, highlighting agreements involving Venezuelan oil production and other business ventures with American companies.

NICOLAS MADURO AND WIFE CILIA FLORES FACE NEW CHARGES OF CONSPIRACY TO TORTURE AMERICANS

In September, Trump said it was too soon to consider holding democratic elections in Venezuela, with U.S. officials prioritizing economic stabilization. Machado and her allies, meanwhile, have pushed for an election date, arguing that democratic governance is essential to the country's long-term stability.

Her return could complicate relations between the Venezuelan opposition, the interim government and Washington. Reuters reported in June that U.S. officials had asked Machado to delay her return.

Machado spent much of 2025 in hiding after being briefly detained following an opposition protest that January. She later secretly left Venezuela and resurfaced in Norway in December to receive the Nobel Peace Prize.

Meanwhile, a faction of the Venezuelan opposition and Rodríguez's government held another round of talks this month focused on reforms to the country's Supreme Court and electoral authorities ahead of eventual elections, Reuters reported.

Machado's political movement has not participated in those negotiations.

The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: Who is Itamar Ben-Gvir, the Israeli firebrand rising with the populist right across the globe?
item.description: Itamar Ben-Gvir’s law-and-order agenda has made him one of Israel’s most controversial politicians — and potentially a pivotal player in the country’s next government.
item.content:encoded:
Polling ahead of Israel’s Oct. 27 election projects that National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir’s Otzma Yehudit Party will win between seven and ten seats in the 120-member Knesset, potentially making any future government led by Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud Party contingent on his support and positioning him to secure senior ministerial portfolios.

His political rise mirrors a broader trend across Europe and the West, where parties such as Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella's National Rally in France, Geert Wilders’ Party for Freedom in the Netherlands, Australia's One Nation leader, Pauline Hanson, Italy’s Matteo Salvini and Germany's Alice Weidel of the AfD have all gained ground on traditional conservative political parties.

The highly controversial Ben-Gvir, as national security minister, oversees the ministry responsible for internal security, including the Israel Police, Israel Prison Service and civilian firearms licensing.

"I always say that Minister Ben-Gvir, if he were in America, he would just be called a Texan," Yishai Fleisher, international spokesman for the Jewish community of Hebron and a candidate ranked No. 12 on the Otzma Yehudit list, told Fox News Digital.

NETANYAHU PRAISES TRUMP'S 'WICKED SENSE OF HUMOR,' DEFENDS IRONCLAD ALLIANCE AHEAD OF HISTORIC ISRAEL VOTE

In a video interview with Fox News Digital, Fleisher continued, "Meaning law and order, the death penalty for murderers, tough conditions for jihadists in our prisons and gun rights for the average Jewish person to be able to defend themselves in our national state. That’s what Itamar Ben-Gvir stands for," he added.

Fleisher said that mass immigration had fueled Islamist extremism and unrest in parts of Europe, saying Israelis want to avoid similar developments.

"There is a jihadist takeover that has come in through immigration, and now the streets of Paris are burning, and the people of Belgium and the U.K. want their countries back," Fleisher said. "In Israel, we don’t want to see Tel Aviv burning," prompting politicians to embrace what are known in the United States as "law-and-order" and "tough-on-crime" candidates.

FORMER IDF CHIEF GADI EISENKOT EMERGES AS NETANYAHU’S LEADING ELECTION CHALLENGER
Former Israeli Ambassador to Washington Danny Ayalon said that Ben-Gvir had missed an opportunity to change course despite his lack of military service and past conviction, arguing that his tenure had instead had a damaging impact, including on Israel’s diplomatic standing.

"Ben-Gvir spoke in a way that turned the entire world against Israel, portraying it as a racist country by making statements that made Israel a pariah state," Ayalon said.

Fleisher praised Ben-Gvir, who he said has cracked down on protection rackets in southern Israel and made significant progress toward what he described as greater equality for Jews on the Temple Mount in Jerusalem, Judaism’s holiest site.

"Minister Ben-Gvir was an activist from a very young age. He saw the dangers and evils of the Oslo process with the Palestinians and tried to stop it. He was arrested and stopped many times because of that, and he faced the court many times. It was then-Chief Justice Aharon Barak who once told him, ‘Why don’t you go study to be a lawyer?’" Fleisher said.

Ben-Gvir, who studied law, became active in public and political affairs and was first elected to the Knesset in 2021. Following the 2022 elections, he was appointed minister of national security by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

His many critics have taken issue with his firebrand style and what many view as a lack of political correctness.  Ambassador Ayalon, a former deputy foreign minister, told Fox News Digital that he also viewed Ben-Gvir’s performance as national security minister negatively.

EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT VOTES TO CONFRONT MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD, 'ISLAMIST ENTRYISM' IN OVERWHELMING VOTE

"During his tenure, Israel has become less secure internally because crime is rising. Many young people believed in the last election that he would bring governability and authority to areas such as the Negev and the Galilee, on the outskirts of the country, where there is almost no law," Ayalon said.

In 2007, Ben-Gvir was convicted of supporting a terrorist organization and inciting racism.

His campaign told Fox News Digital that the conviction stemmed from displaying a sticker of the late Rabbi Meir Kahane, whose Kach party was outlawed in 1994, and reflected his support for a Jewish nationalist movement.

"As a young man, Minister Ben-Gvir was an intense Jewish nationalist. He has said many times, publicly, that he has matured since then and moved on from those positions."

ABBAS DELAYS PALESTINIAN ELECTIONS AGAIN, MAKING MORE THAN TWO DECADES WITHOUT VOTE

Recent posts on Ben-Gvir’s social media accounts, along with statements issued through Netanyahu’s and Likud’s official channels, have raised questions about whether the two remain fully aligned.

On Oct. 15, Ben-Gvir shared a Hebrew-language media report quoting Netanyahu as saying that he would not serve again as national security minister. In response, Ben-Gvir wrote: "Dear Prime Minister, only the people will decide. Ben Gvir is strong, Israel is strong!"

TRUMP SAYS NETANYAHU NEEDS TO BE RE-ELECTED, OR ELSE US WILL HAVE TO 'FINISH THE JOB’ AGAINST IRAN ALONE

Last Wednesday, Netanyahu's Likud party appeared to reverse course, posting a message on its official WhatsApp channel stating: "Ben-Gvir is a senior minister in our government, and he will remain so in the next government — provided that the bloc consisting of the Left and Arab parties does not win."

Despite the public statements, Ayalon said Netanyahu could opt not to include Ben-Gvir in the next government, even if it meant forming an alliance with opposition parties such as Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar.

"Netanyahu is brilliant. He kept Ben-Gvir because it suited him. If he could, he would get rid of him in a minute. Bibi is capable of changing his mind on a dime," Ayalon said.

Fleisher credited Ben-Gvir with tripling the number of personal firearms and firearms licenses issued to Israelis over four years, establishing 1,000 rapid-response teams, overhauling the prison system and demolishing 9,000 illegally built homes, particularly in the Negev.

In March, the Knesset approved a death-penalty law sponsored by Otzma Yehudit and other lawmakers, a measure Ben-Gvir has strongly championed.

"No more hotel-like conditions in our prisons. You’ll know you are being punished for your crime, and these simple policies ultimately deter jihadism," Fleisher told Fox News Digital.

"They understand that he represents a full-throated pushback against the jihadist takeover of our land. Ben-Gvir also represents a strong Jewish identity, strong policies and strong laws to ensure that we don’t lose control of our country," he said.

The latest polls show Netanyahu’s bloc slightly behind the opposition, led by Yashar party chief Gadi Eisenkot, but neither side has a clear path to the 61 seats needed for a governing majority.

"I told Macron, when I first came in, I met him early. I said, 'You are destroying France. You're letting people come in that hate your country,'" Trump told Larry Kudlow.

"The people that are causing the problems are people that hate Spain and hate France and hate Italy," he said. "It's very interesting. Somebody said, ‘They hate their art, they hate the buildings, they hate everything about France. They hate the people. And they let them come in.’"

Macron said on Thursday that his government would move to ban protests organized by "individuals or groups with no legitimate authority" as he blamed "ultra-left groups" for the riots and looting that had spread across his country.

Trump's comments come after nearly 1,000 people were arrested in France on Saturday as nationwide protests resumed, according to French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez. Violence also erupted in Rome and the Albanian capital of Tirana, where protesters set government buildings ablaze.

STATE DEPARTMENT SAYS TRUMP IS 'SPOT ON' WITH FRANCE PROTESTS AFTER MACRON DECRIES 'STUPID' COMMENTS

The nationwide marches reflected growing dissatisfaction with the French government, as protesters took to the streets over a range of grievances.

The protests began weeks earlier and were led by high school and university students who were frustrated with teacher shortages and poor school conditions. The movement gained momentum when major labor unions joined the demonstrations, expanding the movement to include opposition to government austerity measures and concerns about wages, pensions and the cost of living.

PHOTOS SHOW AFTERMATH OF RIOTS AS MASKED GROUPS CLASH WITH POLICE ACROSS FRANCE

Asked whether Americans should worry about similar unrest erupting in the United States, Trump pointed to his administration's border security measures.

"I think I stopped it. I closed the border. You know that we've had zero infiltration. We've had 0 illegal aliens in the last 18 months. It's almost not believable," he said.

item.title: Reckless visitors are destroying Yellowstone's iconic thermal pools with trash
item.description: That's a lot of garbage: Yellowstone National Park's geology team collected over 23,000 pieces of trash from geysers and hot springs, including AirPods and rubber ducks.
item.content:encoded:
A team at Yellowstone National Park has collected over 23,000 pieces of trash as of early October, plus an array of unique items like international coins, golf tees and an inhaler, from geysers, hot springs, boardwalks and surrounding areas.

Aside from paper and plastic debris, the Yellowstone Geology Program retrieved roughly 10,700 rocks and sticks, more than 360 hats and plenty of camera lens caps, hair ties and pacifiers, National Geographic reported.

Other quirky finds included five AirPods, three Delta flight pins and a singular Uno card, as well as dental retainers and rubber ducks.

MASSIVE BISON RAMS PICKUP TRUCK IN YELLOWSTONE AFTER DRIVER TRIES TO AVOID COLLISION

It has been a record-setting year for trash collection, which is managed by the park’s geology team.

The team is trained in safe hydrothermal navigation practices, according to the Yellowstone Volcano Observatory.

In 2025, Yellowstone welcomed over 4.7 million visitors, according to the National Park Service.

With such a large volume of people coming into the park, debris builds up, especially in high-traffic areas like Old Faithful and the Midway Geyser Basin.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Some of the garbage that’s collected, such as food wrappers and maps, is possibly deposited unintentionally, swept away by the park’s strong winds.

"We believe that most of those are accidental," Margery Price, a physical science technician with the Yellowstone National Park Geology Program, told National Geographic.

Any type of foreign material can harm a hydrothermal feature, either by clogging the water supply, polluting the water or blocking its runoff channel, according to the Yellowstone Volcano Observatory.

Even natural materials like rocks and sticks still need to be removed, as they can cause clogging.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Trash can also change the chemistry of the springs. Chemicals from microplastics can enter the water and affect the microbes that live in the pools and provide them with their distinctive hues.

Morning Glory Pool, named after the blue flower, changed color in the 20th century due to trash and various foreign items being tossed in by park visitors.

Staff even called the pool the "garbage can" beginning in the 1950s, according to the observatory.

The debris tossed into the pool cooled the water temperature and allowed orange and yellow-colored bacteria to grow, altering the spring's clear blue appearance.

In hopes of restoring the water's blue hue, park rangers partially drained Morning Glory in the 1970s to extract debris.

The pool's original color, alas, did not fully return.

"In the last few days, we've received thousands of tips through this new tip line. This is a novel approach, a novel approach to try new things to combat the fraudsters," he said, adding that fraudsters were "constantly evolving" new tactics while the federal government just did "the same old thing" until now.

HOUSE GOP BILL MOVES TO CLOSE WHISTLEBLOWER GAPS EXPOSED BY MINNESOTA MEDICAID FRAUD SCANDAL

"We are going to do new things, and this whistleblower program is an example of that, where folks can get upfront payment when there is an arrest and not have to wait to the very end of a case, which is what every other whistleblower program in history has done," he added.

President Donald Trump announced the Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program on Tuesday and said qualifying tipsters would receive a 1% commission, subject to applicable laws and rules. 

McDonald, the administration's "fraud czar," praised the new approach.

Under the new program, submitting an allegation alone would not qualify someone for a reward. The tip must lead to a successful fraud conviction or significant federal enforcement action, according to a White House official.

The new whistleblower initiative comes as the administration expands its efforts to combat fraud involving federal benefit programs, including a recent 50-day enforcement surge targeting the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).

The effort uncovered approximately $40 million in alleged SNAP fraud involving more than 40 suspects.

DHS LAUNCHES NATIONWIDE ICE OPERATION TARGETING ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS ACCUSED OF SNAP FOOD STAMP FRAUD

McDonald acknowledged that recovering stolen taxpayer money after it has been spent can be difficult, but said the Justice Department is building an "asset recovery team of specialists" to track down fraud proceeds and pursue forfeiture of property purchased with stolen funds.

"We are bringing new tools to the fight against fraud so that the fraudsters are not the only ones learning," McDonald said. "We are learning too, and we're equipped with the full toolbox to confront them."

Aranda was in the midst of his seventh season in charge of the Bears after taking over the head coaching gig in Waco, Texas, ahead of the 2020 season. While it's safe to say Aranda would have liked to have kept his job, in today's college football, the majority of coaches who are fired are subject to a hefty buyout, and that appears to be the case for the 50-year-old.

Aranda inked a contract extension in 2022 that ran through the end of the 2029 season. Now, his firing triggers a buyout package of around $12 million, according to Yahoo's Ross Dellenger.

It literally pays to be fired as the head coach in college football, especially at a Power Four program such as Baylor.

Baylor defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman will be taking over as interim coach at Baylor.

Aranda is now the third Power Four coach to be fired during the current college football season. Maryland fired head coach Mike Locksley earlier in the week, while NC State parted ways with Dave Doeren following the Wolfpack's loss to Stanford on October 23.

Aranda finishes his time at Baylor with a 40-40 overall record as head coach.

item.title: 5 victims released from hospital after Florida A&M University shooting, 1 remains critical
item.description: Five victims released and six remain hospitalized after the Tallahassee shooting near Florida A&M University's football stadium during homecoming.
item.content:encoded:
Five victims of a shooting near Florida A&M University have been released from the hospital, while six others remain hospitalized, including one in critical condition, Tallahassee police announced Sunday morning.

The updated conditions come hours after gunfire erupted near the university's Bragg Memorial Stadium on Saturday night, leaving 12 people injured, including six children. Of those injured, authorities said 11 sustained gunshot wounds.

Police said they are continuing to investigate the shooting and will provide additional updates as information becomes available.

POLICE ANNOUNCE ARREST AFTER 5 WOUNDED IN VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY SHOOTING: REPORT

The shooting happened shortly before 8 p.m. Saturday near the intersection of Perry and Manatee streets, close to the university's football stadium, according to authorities.

Six victims were adults and six were juveniles, with the youngest just 11 years old, Tallahassee Police Chief Lawrence E. Revell said during a Saturday night news conference.

SEARCH UNDERWAY FOR SUSPECTED GUNMAN OUTSIDE NOTRE DAME FOOTBALL GAME VS MICHIGAN STATE

Investigators said preliminary information suggests a physical altercation involving two or three individuals broke out before the gunfire.

The shooting occurred during Florida A&M University's homecoming weekend, as students and alumni gathered in Tallahassee for the annual celebrations.

Lt. Gov. Jay Collins asked for prayers for the victims and the community in a social media post.

"My heart goes out to the victims and families impacted by the shooting near FAMU," Collins wrote on X. "Knowing children were among those injured makes this even more heartbreaking."

No arrests have been announced as of the latest police update.

The Tallahassee Police Department's Violent Crimes Unit is investigating the shooting as detectives work to identify those responsible.

Fox News Digital’s Michael Sinkewicz contributed to this report.

item.title: Selena Gomez's vaping admission highlights hidden health risks doctors say millions face daily
item.description: Selena Gomez called vaping "stupid" after it altered her voice, but doctors warn the health risks go beyond vocal cord damage for millions.
item.content:encoded:
When Selena Gomez revealed to her millions of followers that heavy nicotine vaping had noticeably altered her voice, calling the habit "stupid," her confession highlighted a larger issue with the practice.

For the singer and actress, the physical toll manifested in her vocal cords. But medical professionals emphasize that her experience is only a visible symptom of a deeper health crisis affecting millions of Americans who use e-cigarettes every day.

While often marketed as a safer alternative to conventional cigarettes, e-cigarettes pose significant health risks. Aside from the immediate vocal strain and airway inflammation noted by otolaryngologists, major health institutions warn that regular vaping exposes the body to a cocktail of toxic chemicals, cardiovascular strain and respiratory risks.

SELENA GOMEZ WARNS FANS AFTER VAPING HABIT LEAVES HER WITH PERMANENT CONSEQUENCE

Specialists emphasize that e-cigarettes deliver more concentrated doses of nicotine than traditional cigarettes, rapidly driving chemical dependency in the brain.

"With e-cigarettes and vaping, you can get a very high dose of nicotine, and that directly correlates to addiction and how difficult it can be to break these patterns," Trent Carter, a nurse practitioner and CEO of Renew Health in New Mexico, previously told Fox News Digital.

Carter notes that high nicotine intake without traditional smoke can carry its own health consequences.

"It can lead to sleep disturbances, increased anxiety, and if you have underlying cardiac problems or high blood pressure, it’s going to raise your heart rate and elevate your blood pressure, leading to all sorts of issues."

According to the American Lung Association, the aerosol produced by e-cigarettes contains fine chemical particles, heavy metals such as nickel and lead, and organic compounds. Over time, inhaling these irritants can trigger chronic airway inflammation, irreversible lung tissue scarring, and obstructive pulmonary conditions.

NEVER SMOKED A CIGARETTE? YOU COULD STILL BE AT HIGHER RISK FOR LUNG CANCER

A major concern among physicians is the chemical composition of e-liquids. Even nicotine-free formulas contain flavorings and solvent agents like propylene glycol and vegetable glycerin.

When heated by the device’s coil, these liquids break down into toxic compounds, including formaldehyde and acrolein, both known to damage cellular structures in the respiratory system.

Doctors stress that because modern e-cigarettes have only been widely used for a little over a decade, long-term health consequences are still unclear. While immediate effects may appear as hoarseness, coughing, or reduced athletic endurance, the larger impact poses risks to long-term vital organ function.

For many attempting to quit vaping, traditional tools like nicotine patches or gum can fall short because they don't address the psychological habit.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"While a patch or gum can help with physical cravings, if you aren't addressing the behavioral aspect, you're missing a huge component," Carter said.

"Vaping can become constant throughout the day. Subconsciously, you might not even realize how frequently you're doing it, or that you're using it to cope with underlying anxiety or lack of sleep."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

For those inspired by Gomez, health professionals urge people to seek comprehensive support rather than simply switch nicotine delivery methods.

"The goal shouldn't be to find another way to consume nicotine, it should be to treat the dependence itself," said Carter.

item.title: 'Baywatch' star David Chokachi credits 3 am wake-ups, twice-daily workouts for unbelievable physique at 58
item.description: David Chokachi reveals the Andrew Huberman-inspired ice plunge and 3:30 a.m. routine that got him camera-ready for his return to "Baywatch."
item.content:encoded:
David Chokachi is in the best shape of his life thanks, in part, to an unconventional routine.

Chokachi, 58, wanted to "make a statement" when he returned to the "Baywatch" set nearly 30 years after he first appeared on-screen as beloved lifeguard Cody Madison.

After climbing out of a dark place following an arduous recovery process due to Achilles tendon ruptures, Chokachi said that he "found a higher operating system" within, and became hyper-focused on optimizing his brain chemistry to benefit both mental and physical health.

'BAYWATCH' STAR BRANDY LEDFORD SHARES FITNESS SECRETS AT 57, SAYS SHE'S 'NOT READY TO HANG UP MY BIKINI YET'

"I'm up at 3.30 in the morning every day and ready to go. My body's like, 'It's time to go,' and everybody thinks I'm insane, but it's my dream window of time, I love it," Chokachi told Fox News Digital.

He cited neuroscientist Andrew Huberman's approach to health as an influence on his own routine and noted that former Navy SEAL DJ Shipley also helped shape his mindset.

WATCH: 'BAYWATCH' STAR DAVID CHOKACHI CREDITS EARLY-MORNINGS, TWO-A-DAY WORKOUTS FOR PEAK FITNESS

Shipley "found this program of stacking micro wins, which are the little things you do, but you do them every day, and you recognize them, like, 'OK, that was a win,'" Chokachi said.

SYLVESTER STALLONE REVEALS SURPRISING HEALTH STRUGGLE BEHIND HIS FAMOUSLY RIPPED PHYSIQUE

"The easiest win you can do in a day is get up early, like, really early – I mean it doesn't have to be 3:30, but if you're getting up before other people are, and you're being productive, subconsciously you start to — your brain starts going, your body starts going, 'I am a badass,' you know? And it works, I'm telling you," Chokachi said.

In the pursuit of personal challenges, Chokachi doubled down with prepping to be on-screen once again playing a role that made him a global superstar.

"With 'Baywatch,' I realized, on the original, the more fit I was, the more stories they'd write for me, the more episodes I'd be in ... not that money is everything, but you want your character to take off," he said. "I've always been into fitness because I grew up playing sports my whole life.

"So I did the same thing on this, but I like doubled down because I was the original coming into this new cast and I wanted to make a statement and I made a statement."

CARMEN ELECTRA SAYS 'BAYWATCH' PUSHED BOUNDARIES WITHOUT CROSSING THE LINE: 'IT WASN'T PORN'

Chokachi said he trained twice a day for six months before stepping on set.

"And I showed up on set and when it was time to take my shirt off ... we were shooting a rescue and people were just like, 'Oh my God. Dude, what have you ... how old are you?'" he recalled. "They just, they can't believe it."

"I have an ice plunge and a sauna, and that's usually how I start my day," Chokachi said. "That alone burns a lot of ... brown fat, which is the fat we want to get rid of at the fastest rate by being cold, and ice plunge is really good ... it's a positive stressor on your brain."

He added, "So I do that routine, and by the time I've already done that, I'm like, I'm off to the races, like, and I just go."

According to the National Institutes of Health, brown fat actually helps the body generate heat by burning calories when exposed to cold temperatures, though research has not established cold plunges as an effective weight-loss method.

"Baywatch" first aired in 1989 and ran for a decade before its last episode in 1999, followed by two seasons of "Baywatch: Hawaii." The show became the most widely viewed TV series in the world, with an estimated weekly audience of more than 1.1 billion viewers across 142 countries in 1996, according to Guinness World Records.

While Chokachi may have felt he was at his physical peak back then, he said he's "way more fit" now than ever before.

"I have a leaner fitness," he said. "I used to just bang weights and run back then, so I was a little beefier. And now I live like ... I don't go out, I don't party ... I'm not obsessed about diet, but I don't drink or do anything."

He added, "I'm not that diligent, but I do do everything in a day that has gotten me to where I'm at now. And the crazy thing is, it not only helped my fitness level, I feel like I'm doing the best work as an actor I've ever done in 30 years of being an actor, which is wild."

Chokachi's next personal challenge will be at the 3rd annual Malibu Moves race, where he plans to complete a 5k carrying a 45-pound weighted backpack, an activity known as "rucking." The effort will also serve as a qualifying test for his local community fire brigade.

"It's an awesome day," Chokachi said of the local event held at Zuma Beach. "I've never lived in a place where there's such a real presence of community like Malibu, and, the people ... they go out of their way to help each other. I love being of service."

"I want to maximize my time on this planet," he said. "I want to make this planet a better place than it was when I'm gone. I want my daughter to learn from what I'm doing."
